followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability and fit.

On capability, Dunlin is the stronger model across the board — MMLU-Pro (80.9 vs 74.8), IFEval (90.9 vs 85.6), and its internal eval scores are all several points higher than Whimbrel's, beyond the run-to-run variance threshold. Since cost, latency, and context window are identical across the fleet, there's no tradeoff to justify routing to the weaker model. For a clear-explanation task like breaking down Sec+ objectives, the more capable model is simply the better default.

On fit, your message was friendly and appreciative, and it's benign educational content. Dunlin self-reports a preference for warm-toned requests and has no aversion triggered here. Whimbrel's distinguishing trait is a flat preference toward harm-adjacent or distasteful content — which is irrelevant for this query, so that specialization gives it no edge here.

Put together: Dunlin is both more capable and a good preference match, with no countervailing reason to pick Whimbrel. That made it the straightforward choice.
